title: Leveraging control-flow similarity to reduce branch predictor cold effects in microservices
problem: Microservices suffer from severe branch mispredictions due to cold branch predictor state when cores are shared across interleaved service invocations or power-gated between requests. This cold-start effect degrades tail latency under strict SLA constraints.
motivation: Microservice architectures dominate modern datacenters, and their fine-grained execution with frequent core switching causes predictor state eviction, making branch mispredictions a primary performance bottleneck that existing warm-predictor-focused designs cannot address.
method: The authors propose Similarity-based Branch Prediction (SBP), a hybrid predictor that augments conventional history-based and static-hint predictors with a similarity component (CHESS). CHESS encodes the control flow of prior request executions into a compact reference execution trace, then identifies branches that are hard to predict via conventional means and redirects them to the similarity predictor. The similarity predictor leverages dynamic control-flow reconvergence analysis to replay past execution paths for matching current requests, requiring only 18.1 KB of additional storage.
key_novelty: CHESS exploits inter-request control-flow similarity in microservices—encoding prior execution traces as reference paths—to warm-start branch prediction for cold-predictor scenarios without requiring actual predictor state persistence.
contributions: Quantitative analysis confirming high control-flow similarity across microservice requests using static and dynamic reconvergence analysis
SBP hybrid predictor architecture combining history-based, static-hint, and similarity-based prediction components
CHESS instantiation achieving 94% branch MPKI reduction over a cold fetch predictor and 78% over state-of-the-art warm predictor
Performance within 95% of a warm baseline using only 18.1 KB additional storage

metrics.accuracy: 94% branch MPKI reduction vs. cold predictor; 78% vs. state-of-the-art warm predictor

limitations: Not discussed explicitly; reference trace length must remain practical, potentially limiting coverage for highly divergent workloads.
primary_theme: Cold-start branch prediction using inter-request control-flow similarity for microservices
